title: The Model Swap Workshop: GPT-5.5 vs Kimi vs DeepSeek vs Mistral — Pamela Fox, Microsoft
talk_summary: Pamela Fox runs a hands-on comparison of GPT-5.5, Kimi, DeepSeek and Mistral across single calls, RAG grounding, image input, tool calling, agent loops, evals and DSPy prompt optimization. The practical core is: models differ sharply on grounding, parallel tool calls and loop efficiency, so you must evaluate per-scenario and can recover cheap-model quality with prompt engineering or DSPy-compiled prompts.

takeaways.technique: Per-scenario model capability matrix instead of benchmark-based routing
takeaways.what_they_do: They run the same task suite (counting, RAG grounding, image reading, tool-call args, agent loops) against each model and pick per task type, because benchmark scores don't predict scenario behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't really know how good a model is until you use it for your particular scenario
takeaways.numbers: DeepSeek got 6/13 E's, Mistral 8/13, GPT-5.5 and Kimi 13/13 on the counting task

takeaways.technique: Cheap string/arg assertions for tool calls, LLM-judge only for fuzzy output
takeaways.what_they_do: For single tool calls they assert on tool name and argument strings; only for fuzzy outputs do they add an LLM judge that returns pass/fail plus a reason and gets the full trace (tool defs, calls) as context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for tool calls, yeah, that's where you're going to get a bit fancier

takeaways.technique: Calibrate LLM judges against human labels; distrust the judge before the app
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that when an eval fails you must determine whether the app or the judge is wrong, and calibrate judges with domain-expert human labels.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to figure out like wait, is the problem my app or is the problem my judge

takeaways.technique: Measure agent loop efficiency: tool-call count and parallelization per goal
takeaways.what_they_do: They compare models on how many tool calls and turns they need to reach the same goal, and whether they batch independent calls in parallel; some models loop redundantly or drop the final step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the differences between the models is their efficiency. Are they able to get to the goal faster?
takeaways.numbers: GPT-5.5 solved the budget problem in 1 tool call; DeepSeek took 4; Kimi sometimes re-verified after already succeeding

takeaways.technique: DSPy/Jeppa-compiled prompts to make cheap models match expensive ones
takeaways.what_they_do: Declare the spec and output constraints in code, let DSPy hill-climb prompts with a genetic optimizer against those checks, and ship the generated prompt for the cheap model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is a system prompt that works with Mistral ... we can use the cheapest model and still get the results we need

takeaways.technique: Grounding checks: force per-claim source attribution to catch weight-leakage
takeaways.what_they_do: They test whether models answer only from provided sources; weaker models answer from weights, and requiring each claim to cite a source exposes it (though it still leaks).
takeaways.evidence_quote: are the models willing to admit what they don't know, how likely are they to make stuff up?
takeaways.numbers: Mistral answered honey-bee questions from weights despite sources lacking that info
